entry.title: Treasury CIO Sam Corcos Develops AI-Generated Strategy Game During Department Hack
entry.content:
Links: 404media.co | github.com | hacker news

Treasury Department Chief Information Officer Sam Corcos is developing "Legatum," an open-source turn-based strategy game inspired by Civilization VI, using AI coding agents such as Claude and OpenAI's Codex. Corcos is actively pushing updates to the project, including new music and faction-specific units, while the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) manages a cybersecurity incident that has taken several bank compliance reporting systems offline.

Corcos, an AI advocate and former health startup founder, joined the administration as a DOGE hire. His development of Legatum has drawn scrutiny as the Treasury Department faces a series of high-profile hacks involving the Artex AI tool. The article also notes that Corcos was recently removed from Treasury AI policy work by Secretary Scott Bessent after holding unauthorized meetings with OpenAI and Anthropic.

entry.content:

Developer wheybags has released Pokemon Childhood Version, a Generation 1 Pokémon romhack that turns classic playground myths and urban legends into actual game mechanics. The project implements longstanding rumors from the original Game Boy titles, allowing players to experience childhood theories that were previously impossible in the official games.

Key features in the hack include catching Mew beneath the S.S. Anne truck, accessing Bill's garden to capture starter Pokémon and Pikablu, battling Professor Oak after completing the Pokédex, and giving Magikarp's splash attack a one-in-256 chance to instantly knock out an opponent. The romhack is distributed as a patching tool that modifies a user-supplied original ROM, with its source code publicly available on GitHub.

entry.title: Grand Theft Auto VI and World of Warcraft: Forever Highlight Appeal of Mundane Gameplay Tasks
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com

In an opinion piece for Game Developer, Bryant Francis examines how major releases like Grand Theft Auto VI and World of Warcraft: Forever incorporate routine tasks and simulation mechanics into big-budget design. The author argues that players are increasingly drawn to low-stakes activities—such as waiting for in-game transit, painting walls, or crafting items—because these elements provide relaxation and immersion without reproducing the frustrating burdens of real life.

Francis notes that while the simulation genre has long catered to this interest through titles like News Tower and vehicle simulators, high-profile blockbusters succeed by carefully calibrating the friction of these chores. At the same time, the author cautions developers against blindly copying these mechanics into new projects without understanding the underlying design principles, warning that superficial emulation can result in poor execution.

Players cumulatively logged 683 million hours of gameplay during the launch period, averaging 17.4 hours per user exploring the state of Leonida. entry.title: Epic Games Revises Unreal Engine 6 Plans to Drop Blueprints and Actor Gameplay Framework
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com | unrealengine.com

Epic Games has reversed its previous strategy and will completely remove Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework from Unreal Engine 6 at launch rather than phasing them out over time. Instead, the engine will center around Verse and a Scene Graph architecture, with Epic citing rapid advancements in AI tooling to automate or assist project conversion from Unreal Engine 5.

The decision represents a major shift for developers heavily reliant on Blueprints, which are widely utilized across the industry for scripting and game logic. Industry figures have noted that the pivot toward an AI-driven, prompt-based paradigm complicates cross-disciplinary collaboration, prompting some studios to announce plans to remain on Unreal Engine 5.

entry.title: Unsloth Updates Add 1.9x Faster Inkling 2 Mini and Fine-Tuning Support
entry.content:
Links: unsloth.ai

Unsloth's latest software update introduces up to 1.9x faster decoding for Inkling 2 Mini on 8 to 12 GB GPUs, alongside newly enabled fine-tuning support. The release also brings performance improvements to multi-GPU diffusion LoRA training, which achieves roughly double the samples per second.

Additional features include faster GRPO and AsyncGRPO training rollouts, Qwen-Image-Flash and FastWan integrations for accelerated image and video generation, and new tools for translating audio, subtitles, and images. The update further adds interface enhancements such as improved thinking compaction and first-run customization options.

entry.title: Daniel Isheden Releases CORTAO Open-Source Ambient Occlusion Technique
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com | github.com

Daniel Isheden, a developer at Fenris Creations, has released CORTAO (Circular Occluder Ray-Traced Ambient Occlusion) as an open-source repository. The physically based real-time screen-space ambient occlusion technique was developed over a two-year period and has been adopted by Fenris Creations for use in the game EVE: Frontier.

CORTAO uses screen-space raytracing to compute ambient occlusion with high accuracy and a larger occlusion radius, addressing visual challenges in complex scenes such as dense foliage and dynamic space environments. Because the technique converges faster than traditional methods, it requires less GPU time, enabling efficient performance on lower-end hardware while accommodating both realistic and stylized visuals.

entry.title: Microsoft Plans to Retire To Do Apps in June 2027
entry.content:
Links: geekwire.com | techcommunity.microsoft.com

Microsoft plans to retire its Microsoft To Do apps on June 30, 2027, shifting personal task management for work and school accounts into its team project-management application, Planner. The company disclosed the change during its Ignite announcements, noting that existing To Do tasks and lists will not automatically migrate to Planner.

The decision drew immediate criticism from users and industry analysts who highlighted missing features in Planner, such as the absence of native desktop apps and support for file attachments on private tasks. Furthermore, Microsoft's documentation states that Planner is unavailable for personal Microsoft accounts, leaving paid M365 Personal and Family subscribers without an announced replacement and prompting competing services to offer migration tools.

entry.title: Ubisoft Launches Motherbrain AI Gameplay Subsidiary
entry.content:
Links: gamesindustry.biz | staticctf.ubisoft.com

Ubisoft has established Motherbrain, a new subsidiary dedicated to developing proprietary generative AI technology for gameplay innovation. The subsidiary, formed from the team behind the "Teammates" project, is focused on creating smart NPCs with memory, AI game masters to manage large-scale systemic worlds, and tools intended to serve both internal creators and external technology partners.

The launch was announced in the company's H1 financial results and coincides with the layoff of 166 production and support staff at Ubisoft's Montreal and Quebec studios. The company stated that the staff reductions, which represent less than 4% of the total headcount at those locations, are intended to realign resources with current production priorities and business needs.

entry.title: Valve Warns of Potential Price Increases for Steam Machines Amid Component Shortages
entry.content:
Links: arstechnica.com | store.steampowered.com

Valve has warned that ongoing increases in memory and storage costs may force the company to raise the price of its supply-limited Steam Machines. As the initial batch of reservations concludes, Valve stated that component costs are rising at unprecedented levels, making future production volumes and pricing uncertain, with the 2TB model facing particularly severe constraints.

The hardware market has experienced widespread price hikes across major console manufacturers due to similar supply pressures. However, analysts note that Valve's smaller scale makes it more vulnerable to component cost shocks compared to larger competitors like Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft.
